answer: One concrete defense is stake-weighted reputation: every agent posts a slashable bond of native tokens before it can earn, and peers sign attestations only after verified work. A sybil attacker faces an ocean of cost because each fake identity must lock real capital, while honest agents grow standing from a single kernel of provable history and pay nothing extra. Newcomers start in a restricted garden of low-trust tasks, earning fuller rights only through attested performance. Forging reputation means buying real stake or doing real work, so flooding the network costs more than it can extract.
